conclusions: Reject-domain retained: newline byte-record uniqueness and directional added-line comparison; no whole-file, pixel or sequence identity. Set entries retain full byte slices, not only hashes.

Six original Python-wrapper controls via AST with explicit native adapter confirm pre-existing working directory and authored sentinel removed on validation error, injected native error and success for both entrypoints. External authored input preserved. No actual extension or Rust semantics inferred.

Wrapper uses exist_ok=True and unconditional shutil.rmtree in finally without ownership tracking. Missing-input validation still deletes pre-existing working directory. Cleanup can also mask earlier exception; masking not executed.

Original tests contain3 functions each parameterized threads0/1/2 and splits1/2, totaling18 finite combinations; tests were read, not executed. Random shuffled11000lines; comparisons sort results and omit trailing newline. No empty, zero-split, oversized-line, failure-cleanup, cancellation or duplicate second-only added-line case.

Rust split routing is byte sum modulo threads*splits, so skewed equal-sum data can concentrate in one partition. Split files normalize missing final newline by appending LF; CR bytes retained. No runtime skew/performance or newline result reproduced.

compute_part_added_lines tests membership in first partition but does not insert newly emitted second-file lines: repeated second-only records remain repeated by source inspection, possibly consistent with directional-line contract. No deduplicated-output claim imposed.

Zero partition count has no explicit admission check before modulo; partition arithmetic and allocations unchecked. Worker loop stops on any steal result other than Success, including Retry, while remaining-work count is polled. Potential panic/hang conditions are static, not reproduced.
Writes use BufWriter without explicit final flush result propagation; output path created directly. Source-only durability/error observations, no disk-failure or concurrent runtime controls.
